title: Roast Leg of Lamb
subtitle: Herb-studded roast leg of lamb with garlic and rosemary
excerpt: A bone-in leg of lamb studded with garlic and rosemary, roasted to pink and rested well before carving. The centrepiece of the British Easter table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roast leg of lamb is one of the defining dishes of the British Easter table and of French Sunday cooking (gigot d'agneau). Spring lamb is the traditional time for this dish because lambs born in late winter or early spring are slaughtered at about three to four months old in late spring or early summer, producing the mild, tender young meat associated with Easter. The tradition of studding the joint with garlic slivers and rosemary before roasting is the most common British and French preparation. The garlic perfumes the interior of the meat during the long roast. Mint sauce (British tradition) or a jus (French tradition) are the classic accompaniments; redcurrant jelly also works well.

recipeTools.notes: A large roasting tin with a rack.

content.text: Make the incisions for the garlic and rosemary deep enough that the flavourings penetrate into the centre of the joint rather than sitting near the surface where they will burn. For medium-rare, the internal temperature should reach 60 C; for medium, 65 C. A meat thermometer is the most reliable guide. Rest the lamb for at least 20 minutes: it will lose little heat and the juices will distribute far more evenly through the meat.

items.preparation: halved, to rest the lamb on

content.text: Remove the lamb from the fridge 1 hour before roasting. Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Make 20 deep incisions all over the lamb with a small sharp knife. Push a sliver of garlic and a small sprig of rosemary into each hole.

Rub all over with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place on halved onions in a roasting tin. Roast at 220 C for 20 minutes to brown. Reduce to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5 and roast for a further 60 minutes for medium-rare (or until the internal temperature reaches 60 C). Rest for 20 minutes.

While the lamb rests, pour off excess fat from the tin. Place the tin on the hob over medium heat. Add the red wine and scrape up the browned bits. Add the stock and simmer for 3 minutes until slightly reduced. Season and strain into a jug. Carve the lamb and serve with the pan juices.
